results.fact: Avalanche hazard claimed N/A but also described as present in early season
results.correct_value: Avalanche hazard is negligible Jul-Sep once the route is snow-free, but real in the early-season snow gully and on the approach slopes
results.evidence: A south-side trip report describes large winter avalanches that flattened thousands of trees in the basin, plus a couloir that holds a finger of snow toward 8,000 ft. A second route description warns of steep snow on the couloir out of the basin in early summer. The row's own hazards, obj_haz and best_season ('real avalanche exposure' in the Mar-Jun snow window) agree. Only the blanket 'N/A - non-glaciated' zone text contradicts them.

results.fact: Elevation where the two basin entry lines (gully vs ridge) merge
results.evidence: One published route description has the gully out of the ~6,000 ft basin easing at about 6,800 ft. That matches the row's waypoint (6,700) and pitch_detail (~6,800). A second description covers a different line, the couloir toward the Maude col (base of cliffs ~7,200 ft, then a bench ~7,800 ft). That is where the 7,200-7,800 figure in approach, climbing_route[0] and descent_text comes from. Other sources call the gully/ridge convergence a 'flat area' and give no elevation. Only one external source puts an elevation on the merge, so nothing was changed. The likely fix, if a second source turns up: merge at ~6,700-6,800 ft, with the 7,200/7,800 figures kept only for the couloir variant.

results.fact: Distance from the Leroy Creek crossing to Leroy Basin camp
results.correct_value: Leroy Basin camp ~5 mi from the trailhead (3.5 mi to the ford + ~1.5 mi of climbers' path)
results.evidence: One description puts the Leroy Creek crossing 3.5 mi up the Phelps Creek trail (~4,120-4,140 ft), the meadow camp at 6,100 ft, and the round trip at ~13 mi. A trail database gives the Leroy Basin path as 1.4 mi, from 4,160 to 6,121 ft. A third description gives 1.5 mi for the climbers' path. So camp is ~5 mi out, as approach, descent_text, itinerary day 1 and approach_variants all say. One GPS-tracked party logged 6 mi, an outlier. The waypoint distMi values above camp were counted from the wrong 6.0 base, so each drops by the same 1 mi. That puts the summit 6.8 mi one way (~13.6 mi round trip), in line with the ~13 mi round trip.

results.fact: Total cumulative gain/loss (route-level fields vs itinerary day sums)
results.correct_value: ~7,550 ft total gain and loss; summit day ~4,950 ft each way
results.evidence: A GPS-logged trip on this same Phelps Creek / Leroy / Freezer Pass line records 21.5 miles and 7,554 ft of gain, matching gain_ft, loss_ft and totalNote. The row's own waypoint elevations demand it too. Summit day crosses Leroy Pass (6,850) and Freezer Pass (7,600), drops ~1,000 ft to Lower Ice Lake, climbs to 8,392, then climbs back over Freezer Pass on the return, so day 2 cannot be only 3,800 ft. Day 1 becomes 2,600 ft (camp at 6,100 ft; see the discovered Leroy Basin elevation entry, which patches day 1 gain and day 3 loss). Day 2 at 4,950 ft then brings the itinerary total to 7,550 ft, agreeing with gain_ft/loss_ft of 7,554.

results.evidence: The ford is 3.5 mi up the Phelps Creek trail (one description, and the row itself). That fits a GPS-logged 21.5 mi round trip on the same line, so totalNote becomes ~21 miles.

results.fact: dist_km stores the round trip but renders as the one-way approach
results.evidence: dist_km 35.41 km is 22.0 mi, exactly the old itinerary round-trip sum (6.5+9+6.5), yet it renders as 'Approach (one way)'.
